name: Eliab
bio:
Eliab was Jesse's firstborn son, David's older brother. When Samuel came to Bethlehem at the LORD's command to anoint a new king, he saw Eliab's height and commanding presence and assumed he must be the chosen one; but the LORD told Samuel, "Do not consider his appearance or his height, for I have rejected him... the LORD looks at the heart" (1 Samuel 16:6-7), and so Eliab narrowly missed the throne.

Eliab later went with Saul's army to face the Philistines at the Valley of Elah. When David, sent to check on his brothers at the front, was overheard asking about the reward for killing Goliath, Eliab grew angry and rebuked him: "Why have you come down here? And with whom did you leave those few sheep in the wilderness? I know how conceited you are and how wicked your heart is; you came down only to watch the battle." David simply replied, "Now what have I done? Can't I even speak?" (1 Samuel 17:28-29). Eliab's sharp rebuke makes plain the jealousy and condescension he, as the oldest brother who had lost his claim to the throne, harbored toward his youngest brother.
